title: 2010 HMMT February Calculus Problem 2
statement:
Let \(f\) be a function such that \(f(0)=1, f^{\prime}(0)=2\), and

\[f^{\prime \prime}(t)=4 f^{\prime}(t)-3 f(t)+1\]

for all \(t\). Compute the 4th derivative of \(f\), evaluated at 0 .

solutions.text: 54 Putting \(t=0\) gives \(f^{\prime \prime}(0)=6\). By differentiating both sides, we get \(f^{(3)}(t)=4 f^{\prime \prime}(t)-\) \(3 f^{\prime}(t)\) and \(f^{(3)}(0)=4 \cdot 6-3 \cdot 2=18\). Similarly, \(f^{(4)}(t)=4 f^{(3)}(t)-3 f^{\prime \prime}(t)\) and \(f^{(4)}(0)=4 \cdot 18-3 \cdot 6=54\).
